messages:
infra-bot: [ALERT] runtime-prod-gpu-3 high memory pressure (OOMs detected). 12 alerts in 3m. Paging #oncall.

alice_oncall: acked. jumping in — seeing a spike of 5xx / timeouts for customers hitting chat endpoints. any initial obs? @raj_runtime @mei_sre

raj_runtime: I can repro a couple of OOM traces from the runtime logs. attaching snippet:
```
2026-03-15T10:12:02Z runtime[worker-3]: alloc failed: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation
stack: runtime::kv_cache::evict+0x12f
context: batch_size=32, seq_len=1024, model=gpt-open-8k-quant
```
looks like failures correlate with bursty batched requests.

mei_sre: confirmed increased 5xx rate for region=us-west-2 customers. customer-impact: ~18% requests failing in last 10m, elevated latency for non-failing requests (~1.2s -> 2.8s). We should triage live mitigations then work on RCA.

alice_oncall: mitigation checklist: 1) reduce default max batch size 2) disable KV cache for affected pool 3) route traffic to fallback pool (smaller model) 4) scale up nodes. I'll start with (1) & (2).

diego_shiftlead: +1. also notify customer success with ETA. I'll start the handoff doc for next oncall.

alice_oncall: running change — setting max_batch_size=16 for pool runtime-prod-gpu-3 via infra CLI
```
infractl pool update --pool runtime-prod-gpu-3 --max-batch-size 16
```

ops-bot: config change accepted, change_id=c9832, rolling to 4 workers.

raj_runtime: while that's rolling, can we get low-level GPU mem stats? nvml dump coming:
```
GPU 3: total=48GiB free=3.2GiB used=44.8GiB
processes: runtime(pid=2245) 40GiB, runtime(pid=2251) 2.5GiB, model-server(pid=2301) 1.8GiB
fragmentation metric: alloc_retry_count=14, largest_free_block=3.1GiB
```
this smells like fragmentation — largest contiguous block too small for some allocations at high seq_len + batch.

mei_sre: grabbing jemalloc and python-level GC stats from the worker:
```
jemalloc: active=42G mapped=45G retained=6G
python gc: objects=12.3M, last_gc=46s ago
kv_cache: entries=1.2M, mem=12.6G, hit_rate=0.62
```
KV cache is sizable. If eviction logic is causing churn, that could fragment GPU allocation.

alice_oncall: next mitigation — temporarily disable KV cache on that pool to free up contiguous GPU blocks.

raj_runtime: disabling KV cache via rollout flag now.
```
infractl pool feature-toggle --pool runtime-prod-gpu-3 --kv-cache off --rollout 50%
```

ops-bot: rollout started id=roll-7043 target=50% progress=2/4

alice_oncall: customer CS notified: "we're applying traffic mitigations, some requests may be slower as we reroute; ETA 15-30m" :phone: @diego_shiftlead take over customer comms if I need to escalate.

mei_sre: early signals — 5xx rate lowering to 8% and p95 latency dropping. Looks promising.

raj_runtime: collected heap dump + NVML logs to s3://redwood-logs/ooms/1801234567/

alice_oncall: deploying full KV-cache disable on pool (rollout 100%).

ops-bot: rollout complete id=roll-7043 status=success

raj_runtime: after full disable, GPU free contiguous block increased to 9.6GiB, alloc_retry_count -> 0 in recent 2m. No new OOMs reported.

mei_sre: marking customer impact as mitigated, preparing incident page with timeline.

alice_oncall: quick in-thread RCA notes/hypotheses:
- hypothesis A (primary): KV cache eviction pattern + large concurrent batches caused fragmentation; some allocations required contiguous chunks >3GiB so they failed despite high aggregate free memory.
- hypothesis B: quantization path changes for model variant increased peak allocation for certain attention kernels causing transient spikes.
- hypothesis C: jemalloc fragmentation at the process level interacting with CUDA allocator.

alice_oncall: add evidence: nvml largest_free_block before mitigation ~3.1GiB -> after ~9.6GiB; OOM traces reference allocation sizes ~4-6GiB.

raj_runtime: follow-ups I will own:
- add per-allocation tracing around KV cache evict/restore to confirm churn timing
- run synthetic load to reproduce with/without KV cache and varying batch sizes
- try jemalloc tuning (lg_dirty_mult) on a canary node

mei_sre: I will:
- collate logs + timeline into incident doc
- run postmortem timeline and capture customer IDs affected
- verify no other pools show same fragmentation pattern

diego_shiftlead: I'll handle oncall handoff note: summary + links to logs + current mitigations. Oncall for next 12h is @maria_oncall.

alice_oncall: temporary mitigation checklist complete. No more active OOMs. leaving thread for RCA follow-up. If anything new, ping here or escalate to P1.

infra-bot: Incident auto-close check in 30m if no new alerts.

alice_oncall: thanks team. filing an RCA doc and will link here once ready. :white_check_mark:"
